item.title: $p$-Laplace Serrin problem on planar annuli
item.description: arXiv:2610.20861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a rigidity result for the problem $\Delta_p u=-2$ defined on a ring-shaped domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$, when homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed and $p\in(1,2)$. This problem admits a natural physical interpretation, as it describes the steady laminar flow of a generalised Newtonian fluid exhibiting shear-thinning behaviour. Our symmetry result is obtained assuming that the set of maximum points, denoted by $\Sigma$, is a smooth closed curve, and there are no other critical points outside it; moreover, an appropriate asymptotic expansion of the solution near $\Sigma$ is required. Although our approach is inspired by the comparison strategy of [arXiv:2505.04458], the main ingredients used there are intrinsically linear and have no direct counterparts for the $p$-Laplacian. This requires the introduction of new ideas and techniques.
item.dc:creator: Virginia Agostiniani, Chiara Bernardini

item.title: $L^\infty$-regularity thresholds for a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation: dispersive blow-up vs. nonlinear stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.20888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation arising in the mean-field description of exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensates. The dynamics close to macroscopic wave functions $r_0e^{i\omega_0 t +ik_0x}$ is governed by a stabilizing relaxation mechanism without suppressing dispersive blow-up. We show that this competition yields $L^\infty$-regularity thresholds. More precisely, we construct solutions for which arbitrarily small perturbations from $C^4_b$ can develop finite time blow-up in $C^3_b$ whereas perturbations from $C^{4+\eta}_b$ for every $\eta>0$, satisfy a global-in-time $C^3_b$-stability estimate. The stability analysis is carried out in modulation spaces $M_{\infty,1}^k$.
item.dc:creator: Joannis Alexopoulos

item.title: Radiation Conditions and Uniqueness Theorems for Open Wave-guide Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic Maxwell equations. To analyze Maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the Mourre estimates from [29, 32].
item.dc:creator: Charles L. Epstein, Rafe Mazzeo, Solomon Quinn, Andras Vasy

Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $\chi_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $ eta$ and the domain size on the bifurcation. Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $ eta_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $ eta_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $ eta_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $ eta$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $ eta$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns. Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.
item.dc:creator: Le Chen, Ian Ruau, Wenxian Shen

item.title: A Physical-Space Approach to Modified Scattering for the 3D Hartree Equation: Full-Space and Robin Half-Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.21002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation for small data in $H^{0,k}$, with $k>\frac12$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and $k=1$ on the half-space $\mathbb R^3_+$ with a real Robin boundary condition. For these data, the nonlinear and asymptotic analysis is carried out entirely in physical space, combining slow-growth estimates for Galilean vector fields with a scale-invariant interaction estimate. For the half-space problem, we construct an extension intertwining the Robin and free flows and a boundary-adapted field that overcome the loss of normal Galilean symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Pausader, Mengyi Xie

item.title: The Brezis-Nirenberg-type problem for critical cooperative and non-cooperative elliptic systems with general subcritical perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Brezis--Nirenberg-type problem for a class of critical cooperative and non-cooperative elliptic systems with general subcritical perturbations. The system couples two equations through a matrix whose off-diagonal entries may be of either sign, a critical Sobolev-type nonlinearity, and a perturbation that may change sign.The main difficulties are threefold: the linear part is governed by a matrix, the critical nonlinearity couples the two components, and the perturbation is general and may change sign. We prove an abstract existence result under the energy threshold condition and verify this condition in two regimes. For $N\ge4$ the condition holds for every admissible triple, in both the unperturbed and the perturbed case; the proof uses a new $L^{q}$ estimate for the normalized Aubin--Talenti functions, which controls the negative part of the perturbation. For $N=3$ the eficit in the Sobolev quotient is only of order $\eps^{1/2}$, so a stronger linear threshold condition is required; we establish it explicitly for a ball and, for a general bounded smooth domain, in terms of an abstract constant from the classical Brezis--Nirenberg theory. We also establish the system Sobolev inequality with the same constant as in the scalar case. Since the unperturbed case is included, our results extend the classical theory to cooperative and non-cooperative critical systems with general lower-order perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Guanwei Chen

item.title: A class of sum Hessian quotient equations arising in conformal geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.21106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence result of $(n-1)$-admissible solutions to a class of sum Hessian quotient equations with the modified Schouten tensor on Riemannian manifolds. By establishing uniform a priori estimates, we prove the solvability of the problem via degree theory.
item.dc:creator: Ni Xiang, Yuni Xiang

item.title: A Quantitative Hydrodynamic Limit for the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck/Navier-Stokes System in the Fine Particle Regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.21119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We justify the hydrodynamic limit of the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation coupled with the incompressible Navier--Stokes equation in the fine regime with a quantitative convergence rate. In this regime, the limiting dynamics is described by the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes system for the fluid-particle mixture. In contrast with the existing relative entropy approaches, the present work extends to a pointwise convergence of the hydrodynamic limits with an explicit rate on any given time interval [0,T]. The proof is based on a Macro-Micro decomposition around the moving local Maxwellian, together with an $\varepsilon$-weighted energy-dissipation structure adapted to the fine particle relaxation scales. Furthermore, we remove the classical small background restriction inherent in high-order energy methods, allowing the limiting profile to be possibly large. This is accomplished by exploiting a hidden Kelvin-Voigt type damped wave equation structure within the macroscopic velocity error system, yielding the critical extra dissipation required to close the uniform estimates.
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Fang, Jian Li, Kunlun Qi, Huanyao Wen

item.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
item.description: arXiv:2610.21124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Sifan Yu

item.title: Rigidity for formally determined point source scattering for an anisotropic acoustic medium
item.description: arXiv:2610.21258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider an acoustic medium, occupying three dimensional space, whose anisotropic sound speed is modeled by a Riemannian metric which is Euclidean outside a compact region $D$. The medium is probed by acoustic waves generated by a finite number (dimension dependent) of point sources outside $D$ and the medium response is measured on the boundary of $D$ for a finite time period. We show that if these measurements agree with that of an Euclidean metric then the metric is Euclidean up to a diffeomorphism. This result is similar to the result in \cite{ORS26a} where they used plane waves instead of point sources. Using point sources instead of plane waves presents new difficulties, dealt with in this article.
item.dc:creator: Pradipta Chatterjee, Rakesh, Abhilash Tushir

item.title: Time Delay of KPP Fronts Across a Semipermeable Barrier
item.description: arXiv:2610.21322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a KPP reaction--diffusion equation on the real line with a semipermeable barrier at the origin, where the flux is continuous and the density jump is proportional to the spatial derivative. With diffusion and linear growth normalized to one, let $\beta$ denote the barrier resistance. For initial data equal to one sufficiently far to the left and zero near the barrier and on the receiving side, we prove convergence on the receiving side to a minimal-speed wave with a unique phase in the Bramson frame. The difference between distant first-arrival times with and without the barrier therefore has a finite limit $\tau_\beta$, independent of the arrival level and continuous in $\beta$. For concave KPP reactions, this delay is strictly increasing in $\beta$ and satisfies $\tau_\beta=K\beta+o(\beta)$ as $\beta\downarrow0$, with $K>1/4$. Without the concavity assumption, the strong-barrier expansion is $\tau_\beta=\frac12\log\beta-\frac12\log\log\beta+C+o(1)$, where $C$ is determined by the homogeneous reference amplitude and the closed donor-side Neumann evolution. The analysis relates the sustained interface input to the front phase through leading-edge estimates, interior matching, and parameter-uniform moment bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yantao Wang

item.title: Directional delays and singular strong-barrier limits for Fisher--KPP propagation across a semipermeable interface
item.description: arXiv:2610.21328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Fisher--KPP propagation from compactly supported data across a planar semipermeable interface in $N\ge2$ dimensions, with unit diffusion and $f'(0)=1$. For every finite resistance, the receiving front has speed $2$ and logarithmic correction $-(N+2)\log t/2$. Its phase is determined by a positive directional amplitude on the closed receiving hemisphere. This amplitude is jointly continuous in resistance and direction and is H\"older continuous in direction with exponent $1/3$. It also determines a threshold-independent signed arrival-time difference. Under concavity, the amplitude decreases strictly with resistance. As the resistance $\beta$ tends to infinity, the amplitude is asymptotic to $2(4\pi)^{-N/2}I_N(\theta)(\log\beta)/\beta$ uniformly on each fixed receiving cone bounded away from the equator. Here $I_N$ is a weighted input moment of the closed Neumann donor problem. Although this moment diverges logarithmically near the equator, the equatorial amplitude tends to half the amplitude of the even Neumann donor solution. The strong-resistance and equatorial limits therefore do not commute. The proof combines critical derivative moments, an integrated Robin trace estimate, Cartesian leading-edge limits, and matching through the wave displacement. The phase and asymptotic formulas require only the smooth KPP assumptions, without the additional restriction $f'\le f'(0)$. Concavity is used for strict resistance ordering and the strict bounds on the limiting equatorial delay.
item.dc:creator: Yantao Wang

item.title: Higher-order necessary conditions for nonscattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.21338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the scattering of incident waves by a class of planar analytic inhomogeneities with constant refractive index, governed by the Helmholtz equation. We derive an infinite hierarchy of necessary conditions for nonscattering: any complex analytic nonscattering incident wave must satisfy infinitely many differential constraints at a specific point determined by the geometry of the inhomogeneity. As an application, we show that for any noncircular elliptical inhomogeneity, every single separated (Mathieu) mode necessarily scatters. This is in stark contrast to the circular case, where single separated (Bessel) modes are nonscattering at infinitely many wavenumbers.
item.dc:creator: Narek Hovsepyan

item.title: Turing bifurcation, criticality, and multistability in a nonlocal advection-reaction-diffusion equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers a nonlocal advection--reaction--diffusion equation with logistic growth. We investigate how the interaction kernel affects the criticality of Turing bifurcations and the associated multistability. We first prove that nonhomogeneous stationary solutions bifurcate from the positive homogeneous stationary solution. Center manifold reduction yields an amplitude equation near the bifurcation point. This equation provides criteria for supercritical and subcritical bifurcations in terms of the Fourier transform of the interaction kernel. We also derive a sufficient condition for subcriticality. This condition can be satisfied by sufficiently localized attractive interactions. Based on these analytical results, we investigate multistability through numerical bifurcation analysis. The numerical results show that the stable homogeneous stationary solution can coexist with stable nonhomogeneous stationary solutions or stable time-periodic solutions.
item.dc:creator: Yui Nagayama, Masaharu Nagayama, Hiroshi Ishii

item.title: A quantitative Robin P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} theorem for tangential polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.21417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the quantitative Dirichlet theorem of Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} to Robin torsional rigidity. For every fixed $\beta>0$, we prove that the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes Robin torsional rigidity among tangential $N$-gons of prescribed area. Our explicit perimeter deficit bound contains the Dirichlet deficit obtained by Gui, Hu, and Li \cite{GuiHuLi2026} and an additional Robin term that is positive for nonregular tangential polygons. For triangles, we answer the fixed-area optimization problem recorded as open by Keady and Wiwatanapataphee \cite[Appendix A.1.2]{KeadyWiwatanapataphee2016}. We also establish strict monotonicity along equal-area regular polygons as the number of sides increases, with an explicit bound for each consecutive gap. The proof combines mixed Robin--Neumann triangular cells, spectral estimates for angular concavity, and a quantitative scaling estimate.
item.dc:creator: Changfeng Gui, Yeyao Hu, Qinfeng Li, Hang Yang

item.title: Strict unimodality of the exact time-domain diffuse-light response under a Robin boundary condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.21431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-domain boundary measurements of diffuse light are temporal point-spread functions whose peak position is used as a robust scalar datum in diffuse optical and fluorescence imaging. We consider the exact response generated by a single fluorescent point target in a homogeneous half-space with a Robin boundary condition. The response is a temporal convolution of two diffusion Green-function factors containing a complementary-error-function boundary correction. For every positive diffusion, absorption, depth, and source--target and detector--target distance parameter, and for every nonnegative Robin parameter, we prove that the normalized exact response is a generalized gamma convolution density. Its extension by zero to the negative half-line is bell-shaped. A differentiable small-time expansion, established by sectorial analyticity and Cauchy estimates, together with the sign-change structure of the first two derivatives, excludes tangential critical points and yields a unique peak with strict increase before it and strict decrease after it. The argument is exact and requires no large-distance, source--detector balance, symmetry, restricted-time, or small-parameter assumption. The same conclusion holds after convolution with an exponential fluorescence-lifetime density for every positive lifetime. The key ingredients are an explicit Stieltjes representation of the Robin factor, hyperbolic complete monotonicity, closure of the generalized gamma convolution class, and bell-shape theory. A derivation of the exact half-space model and the differentiated endpoint asymptotics are included in two appendices.
item.dc:creator: Junyong Eom, Jinwan Park

item.title: Lifetime-unified quadratic and cubic approximations of fluorescence peak time for a time-domain diffuse-light response
item.description: arXiv:2610.21443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the temporal maximum of a boundary response generated by a coupled diffusion system in a half-space with Robin boundary conditions and a point fluorophore. The fluorescence lifetime enters through a one-sided exponential time convolution. Previous peak-time approximations were derived under separate short- and long-lifetime scalings. We construct a single reduced peak-time formula for every positive ratio of lifetime to the intrinsic width of the transport peak, thereby describing the transition between these regimes without switching formulas. Starting from a known large-distance approximation of the zero-lifetime response, we normalize at its unique maximum and approximate its logarithm quadratically. The resulting scalar mode equation has a unique solution, expressed through the inverse scaled complementary error function. Its endpoint expansions recover the leading structures of the earlier approximations in the corresponding joint large-distance regimes. A cubic correction accounts for the leading local asymmetry. Under a stated bound on the normalized cubic coefficient, we prove uniqueness of its positive mode and agreement with the exact reduced-profile peak expansion through second order in the lifetime. A conditional peak-location stability estimate is combined with a decomposition into transport-profile and local truncation errors. Numerical comparisons with the full diffusion response support the accuracy of the construction. The lifetime-unified formula is distinguished from the fixed-geometry, infinite-lifetime limit, in which the transport tail yields a different peak-time growth law.
item.dc:creator: Junyong Eom

item.title: Fixed-spinor radial solutions of a perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the perturbed Euclidean spinorial Yamabe equation \[ D_{g_{\mathbb R^n}}\psi = \frac n2\bigl(1+\varepsilon K(x)\bigr) |\psi|^{2^*-2}\psi \qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^n,\quad n\ge2, \]where $2^*:=2n/(n-1)$, $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter and $K$ is a prescribed radial function. We establish a finite-dimensional reduction within a radial spinor space determined by a fixed unit spinor, reducing the problem to the analysis of a function of the dilation parameter. Under suitable assumptions on $K$, we obtain explicit existence criteria for solutions with this prescribed spinorial structure, together with a multiplicity criterion yielding solutions associated with distinct scales. These criteria are expressed in terms of the behavior of $K$ at the origin and weighted integral quantities.
item.dc:creator: Ting Li, Zhongwei Tang, Yuhang Zhang

item.title: Global Well-Posedness for the 3-D Inviscid Oldroyd-B Model with Fractional Stress Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.21473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the 3-D incompressible inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion \((-\Delta)^\beta\tau\) and without stress damping. For $\beta \in (\frac{1}{2},1)$ and $s\in [2\beta+\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2}]$, we establish local well-posedness for initial data $(u_0,\tau_0)$ in \(H^s(\mathbb R^3)\), provided that \(\|(u_0,\tau_0)\|_{H^\beta}\) is bounded and \(\|\Lambda^\beta(u_0,\tau_0)\|_{H^{s-\beta}}\) is sufficiently small. If, in addition, $\beta\in(\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{6}]$, we give a global well-posedness result. Our results complement the work of Constantin, Wu, Zhao and Zhu \cite{ConstantinWuZhaoZhu2021} by treating the Sobolev regularity $s\in[2\beta+\frac12,\frac{5}{2}]$, below the threshold $s>\frac52$ considered there. We also provide an $\ell^2$ alternative to the high-frequency $\ell^1$ summability condition in the framework of Wu and Zhao \cite{WuZhao2022}.
item.dc:creator: Yi Lu, Chen Liang, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: On micro-macro derivation of traffic flow models with $(A,B)$-connection and its stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.21519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that $(A,B)$-connections for conservations laws with a flux discontinuity can be obtained as limits of perturbed Follow-the-Leader (FtL) models, and provide continuity and surjectivity of the map associating the perturbation of the dynamics with the flux limiter.
item.dc:creator: F. Ancona, P. Cardaliaguet, A. Cesaroni

item.title: The Bardos-Tartar Conjecture for the Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the incompressible viscous Navier-Stokes equations in dimension $d=2,3$ with periodic boundary conditions and time-independent external forcing. When $d=2$, the Bardos-Tartar conjecture asks whether the set of solutions at any given positive time is dense in the Hilbert subspace of $L^2$ consisting of mean-zero divergence-free vector fields, with respect to the strong $L^2$ norm. We prove the Bardos-Tartar conjecture and, more generally, its analogue for the hyperviscous Navier-Stokes equations studied by Guo-Titi. In addition, for $d=2,3$ we show that any given initial condition is either backwards-extendable (i) for all values of viscosity $\nu>0$, or (ii) only for viscosities that belong to a Lebesgue-null subset of $\mathbb{R}_+$. When (i) holds, we show the initial condition and forcing must be real-analytic (in fact, both belong to $D(e^{\sigma A})$ for some $\sigma>0$, where $A$ is the Stokes operator). Furthermore, we show that (i) is extremely unstable under perturbations. In particular, given any initial condition we show that two Fourier modes can be perturbed so that (ii) holds.
item.dc:creator: Douglas Barnes, Samuel Liew, Edriss Titi

item.title: Spectral Theory for Schrodinger Operators with Interface Transmission Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfaces influence transport across biological membranes, habitat boundaries, and composite media. Motivated by these applications, we study two classes of Schrodinger eigenvalue problems with transmission conditions allowing jumps in the solution or its normal derivative. We develop a weighted variational framework that accommodates asymmetric interface coupling and yields self-adjoint realizations in suitable weighted Hilbert spaces. For both problems and their adjoints, we establish discrete spectra, variational eigenvalue characterizations, and eigenfunction completeness in arbitrary spatial dimensions. We prove spectral continuity and identify limiting spectra in singular parameter regimes. We also extend Courant's nodal domain theorem to eigenfunctions that may be discontinuous across the interface. The spectral results further extend to divergence-form elliptic operators under suitable assumptions on the coefficients. These results provide a foundation for analyzing elliptic and parabolic equations with interface transmission conditions.
item.dc:creator: Linlin Su, Yantao Wang, Zhannan Zhuang

item.title: Generic Mean Curvature Flow With Rough Weights
item.description: arXiv:2610.21545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the generic existence of mean curvature flows in spaces with rough weights. Our weak solutions are both unit-density Brakke flows and distributional solutions. Such a generic statement is optimal in the sense that we consider weights that are too rough to have well-defined traces on every hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Fabius Kr\"amer, Tim Laux, Keisuke Takasao

item.title: Interior Regularity for Stable Solutions of Semilinear Elliptic Equations with Sign-Changing Nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2610.21641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate interior regularity for stable solutions of the semilinear elliptic equation $-\Delta u=f(u)$ in an open set $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb R^n$, where $f$ is locally Lipschitz and may change sign. We establish sharp interior H\"older estimates for stable classical solutions in every dimension $n\le 9$, thereby fully resolving a question raised by Cabr\'e concerning interior regularity without the nonnegativity assumption on $f$. For $n\le 5$, we also give a short alternative proof of the corresponding H\"older regularity result due to Peng, Zhang, and Zhou. We further establish higher-integrability estimates for the gradient and $L^1$ bounds for the Hessian in all dimensions. For $n\ge 10$, we obtain BMO and Morrey estimates, extending related results previously established for nonnegative nonlinearities. When $f$ is convex, we extend the interior regularity estimates to stable weak solutions through an approximation theorem. As applications, we prove Liouville-type theorems for entire stable solutions of equations with sign-changing nonlinearities across all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Long-Han Huang, Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou

item.title: Boundary Harnack inequalities for the fractional $p$-Laplacian in Reifenberg flat domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.21689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a scale-invariant boundary Harnack inequality and H\"older continuity up to the boundary of quotients of positive fractional $p$-harmonic functions in Reifenberg flat domains with sufficiently small flatness constant, for $0<s<1$ and $2\le p<2/(1-s)$. The solutions are globally nonnegative, vanish on a common exterior boundary patch, and belong to the natural local energy and $(p-1)$-tail class. Their distant exterior values may be unrelated and unbounded. After normalization at a corkscrew point, the comparison and H\"older constants depend only on $n,s,p$. We first establish local half-space boundary comparison for every $p\ge2$ and prove relative approximation by the half-space profile in Reifenberg domains. The compactness argument identifies escaped exterior mass and excludes its constant source term. Interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity then yields gradient non-degeneracy and lower increment bounds in a cone of directions. To treat the degenerate kernels produced by linearization, we develop estimates for weighted non-local forms and prove a localized Harnack inequality for bounded quotients, retaining the full exterior interactions. Ordered variational deformations and a common fractional $p$-harmonic majorant yield comparison for solutions with unrelated exterior data. Truncation of distant data and fractional $p$-harmonic replacement extend the estimates from the variational energy class to the natural tail class.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om

item.title: Recovery of coefficients in a Schr\"{o}dinger system with nonlinear coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.21715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of Schr\"{o}dinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. We first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. Then, we show that the linearized Neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. The proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (CGO) solutions for the linear Schr\"{o}dinger equation. We conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of Carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Arrepu, Hanming Zhou

item.title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schr\"odinger operator $(-\Delta)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{\gamma+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $\gamma>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $\gamma+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Lianfeng Yang

item.title: A multi-point maximum principle to prove the global Harnack inequality for the doubly nonlinear heat equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work aims to present a new proof of the global pointwise Harnack inequality satisfied by positive viscosity solutions of the doubly nonlinear heat equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approach is based on a multi-point maximum principle argument introduced by the authors in a recent article [Calc. Var., 2026]. Required for the proof is a new variation of the maximum principle for semicontinuous functions, which is a standard tool in the analysis of viscosity solutions. In particular, our techniques provide a new proof of the Harnack inequalities satisfied by positive solutions of the porous medium equation and the $p$-heat equation, which were derived by Auchmuty and Bao [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 1994] using results of Aronson and B\'enilan [C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, 1979] and Esteban and V\'azquez [Arch. Rational Mech. Anal., 1988]. The results contained in this article have also been discussed in the third author's doctoral thesis.
item.dc:creator: Ben Andrews, Daniel Hauer, Jessica Slegers

item.title: A sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear Schr\"odinger equations on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2610.21734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear Schr\"odinger equations on the real line. We establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. This criterion is formulated in terms of the Mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. To prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the Mizohata condition. To prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.
item.dc:creator: Toshiki Kondo, Mamoru Okamoto

item.title: Moment Propagation for the Vlasov--Poisson System with Gyroscopic Forces, Velocity Diffusion, and Specular Reflection
item.description: arXiv:2610.21745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the three-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with gyroscopic forces and velocity diffusion. For the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ and the specular--Dirichlet problem in bounded domains, we prove the propagation of velocity moments of order $k>2$ for weak solutions with bounded $L^1\cap L^{\infty}$ norms and kinetic energy. The proof applies Serre's compensated integrability to weighted mass--momentum tensors to derive density estimates. A finite iteration alternating moment propagation with improved density integrability then closes the estimates. These estimates provide a simplified approach to moment propagation and yield global continuation of classical solutions.
item.dc:creator: Jingpeng Wu
